name: Fukuoka Airport
before:
Kyushu's principal airport, only 3 km east of Hakata Station, and fourth busiest in Japan with 25 million passengers in 2018. The subway from the domestic terminal reaches the business district in about ten minutes, which makes this one of the most convenient airports in the country.

There is a catch, and it is a big one. The international terminal is on the far side of the runway from the domestic terminal and is only reachable by road. A connecting passenger has to take the inter-terminal bus, so allow real time for it. Buses also run from the international terminal to Hakata Station and Tenjin.

Two other constraints follow from the airport being inside the city. There is a mandatory curfew from ten at night until seven in the morning at the request of local residents, and the airport has been designated congested since March 2016, with slot restrictions. A second runway opened in March 2025 to ease that.

Skytrax ranked it 26th in the world for 2024 and second among regional airports.
after:
Kyushu's principal airport, close to the heart of Fukuoka. The subway from the domestic terminal reaches the business district in about ten minutes, which makes this one of the most convenient airports in the country. It handled 28.8 million passengers in the year to March 2026.

There is a catch. The international terminal is across the runway and the subway serves only the domestic side, so connecting passengers must take the free shuttle bus. Allow time: the airport warns that it is extremely crowded from 8.30 to 9.30am. Buses also run from the international terminal to Hakata Station and Tenjin.

Being so close to the city brings a curfew from 10pm to 7am and, since March 2016, designation as a congested airport. A second runway opened in March 2025 to ease that.

Skytrax ranked it 18th in the world for 2026 (23rd in 2025) and second among regional airports.
